blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — isolation and transmission-based precautions for seasonal influenza
stem: A hospitalized client has laboratory-confirmed seasonal influenza and is coughing frequently. Which infection-control plan is appropriate during routine care?

options.A: Use Standard plus Droplet Precautions; have HCP wear a facemask on room entry, and mask the client during transport if possible.
options.B: Use Standard plus Airborne Precautions for routine bedside care, with a fit-tested N95 and negative-pressure room until symptoms resolve.
options.C: Use Standard plus Contact Precautions for routine bedside care, with gown and gloves for each room entry because fomites are the main route.
options.D: Use Standard Precautions alone after antiviral therapy starts, adding Droplet Precautions only during coughing episodes or procedures.

rationale: A is correct. Current CDC guidance for suspected or confirmed seasonal influenza in healthcare settings requires Standard Precautions and Droplet Precautions. CDC states that healthcare personnel should don a facemask when entering the patient's room and that, if transport is necessary, the patient should wear a facemask if possible. Droplet Precautions are generally continued for 7 days after illness onset or until 24 hours after fever and respiratory symptoms resolve, whichever is longer, with longer duration considered in selected patients such as young children or severely immunocompromised patients. B is incorrect for routine care because airborne infection isolation and fitted N95 respiratory protection are additional measures used for aerosol-generating procedures when feasible, not the default routine-care plan. C is incorrect because influenza is not managed with Contact Precautions as the routine transmission-based precaution and CDC does not identify fomites as the main transmission route. D is incorrect because antiviral treatment does not end transmission precautions; CDC notes that people receiving influenza antivirals can continue shedding virus while on treatment.
educational_objective: Apply Standard plus Droplet Precautions for routine care of hospitalized clients with suspected or confirmed seasonal influenza, while recognizing that aerosol-generating procedures require additional respiratory-protection measures.

correction_summary: Original Q0013 used absolute-word distractors and imprecisely described the facemask as being needed only during close care. The item was rebuilt to mirror current CDC wording: HCP facemask on room entry, patient source control during transport if possible, Standard plus Droplet Precautions for routine care, and separate additional precautions for aerosol-generating procedures. All four options are now realistic transmission-based precaution plans with balanced lengths.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly matches CDC routine-care Standard plus Droplet Precautions, HCP facemask on room entry, and patient facemask during transport if possible.
option_audit.B: Plausible respiratory-protection overreach; incorrect because N95/AIIR measures are tied to aerosol-generating procedures and are not the default routine-care isolation plan for seasonal influenza.
option_audit.C: Plausible surface-transmission overreach; incorrect because routine influenza management uses Droplet rather than Contact Precautions, and contact/fomite spread is not the main route in CDC guidance.
option_audit.D: Plausible treatment-response shortcut; incorrect because antiviral therapy does not immediately stop viral shedding or replace required transmission-based precautions.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on all/only/always/never/must/every-type absolute wording.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths: A 128, B 137, C 140, D 134 characters; the correct answer is the shortest by a modest margin and there is no positive length cue.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four options use parallel Standard-plus-transmission-based-precaution structures and plausible PPE/isolation rationales.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified in the pre-stage audit. B applies aerosol-procedure measures to routine care, C substitutes Contact for Droplet Precautions, and D incorrectly treats antiviral initiation as ending transmission precautions.
